Necromancer · Theorycraft

Blood Lance Necromancer

core-skill blood caster

Necromancer theorycraft unchanged core-skill blood caster confidence medium PTR

Last verified 2026-08-09 • Season 15 (PTR)

Move on when[ptr] Level 70 and Torment 1 - or, on the PTR, whenever Mrak hands them to you - and a first Essence-per-second reading taken.
Move on when[ptr] Essence measurably cheaper than the meta bar and Intelligence visibly converting. If either fails, stop.
Move on when[ptr] The head-to-head is done and this build is at least competitive on packs.

Skill bar

1Reap
2Blood Lance
3Blood Wave
4Sever
5Bone Prison
6Blood Mist

Rotation

[ptr] Blood Lance from range as the main cast, Blood Wave when Overpower needs regaining, Sever and Blood Mist to move, Bone Prison on anything tanky. Watch Essence: the whole hypothesis is that this bar does not drain it the way the meta bar does.

Skill point priority

  1. [ptr] Blood Lance first and maxed - the inversion this build is named for
  2. Blood Wave kept low on the bar as the Overpower regain, which is the mirror image of the meta build's arrangement
  3. Bone Prison for attack speed
  4. Sever, Blood Mist and Reap for movement, corpses and Essence
  5. [ptr] Intelligence over Essence Regeneration wherever they compete - that is the entire gearing thesis and it should be visible from the first endgame piece

Rotation

[ptr] Blood Lance held down, Blood Wave on the Overpower cycle, everything else as before. This is where the two measurements get taken: Essence per second, and damage before and after stacking Intelligence.

Skill point priority

  1. [ptr] Blood Lance maxed with its Overpower, Fortify and Festering Wound upgrades
  2. Blood Wave held at the rank that keeps the Overpower regain working
  3. Bone Prison maxed
  4. [ptr] Gear for Intelligence and multipliers. If you find yourself chasing Resource Cost Reduction again, the hypothesis is failing and the meta build is the better character

How to run them

[ptr] 3.2.0 changes nothing about mercenaries, so this is the Season 14 guidance carried over and labelled as such. Every Necromancer source agrees on Raheir with Bastion reinforcing. The hire is contested even on live - Maxroll switches Aldkin to Subo at the midgame, Icy Veins uses Varyana - and Aldkin is taken here for the flat critical strike chance, which a build with a freed affix budget can convert better than the meta build can. The picks above are what can be stated without inventing an allocation - no payload publishes an Aldkin tree for a Necromancer - so they are his Perk, which is granted rather than chosen, and the one Aldkin skill this repo's knowledge base names. The rest of his tree is left open.

Summary

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] Untested theorycraft: nobody publishes this build for 3.2.0, and nobody publishes any Necromancer build for 3.2.0 at all. The argument is narrow and mechanical. 3.2.0's only real gift to Necromancer is the core-stat scalar going from 1.25 to 1.625, a flat 30% on baseline damage per 10 Intelligence. A scalar buff is worth most to the build that can actually spend its affix budget on the core stat - and the class's meta build cannot, because Blood Wave as a Core skill is resource-hungry enough that its published gearing is dominated by Essence Regeneration, Resource Cost Reduction and Lucky Hit restore tempers. Blood Lance is already in that build, as the Overpower-stack spender, and it is not the thing eating the resource budget. This page asks what happens if it is promoted from spender to carry. There is one piece of outside evidence, and it is Season 14 rather than 3.2.0: InfinityBuilds' 2026-08-02 list carries a Blood Lance Necromancer in A tier, titled 'Core Blood Tide Pit 139/Tower 134'. That is a real person clearing real content with the archetype on the live patch - it is not evidence about 3.2.0 and it is not a build guide this page could read, because the site's build pages are JavaScript-rendered.

Reasoning

Hypothesis[ptr] A 30% core-stat scalar buff is worth more to a build that can afford to gear for the core stat. Blood Wave converts the 3.2.0 Necromancer scalar poorly because its own resource cost forces Essence Regeneration, Resource Cost Reduction and Lucky Hit restore rolls into most of its contested affix slots - the published gates are over 15 Essence Regeneration and over 25% Resource Cost Reduction before Ring of Starless Skies. Blood Lance sits in the same build already, costs less to cast, and is not what the resource gates were written for. Promoting it to the carry skill should free most of the jewelry budget for Intelligence and multipliers, which is exactly where a +30% scalar pays.
Confidencemedium
How to test it[ptr] (1) Measure Essence per second spent with Blood Lance as the carry versus Blood Wave as the carry, on the same character. The whole argument is that the first number is much smaller; if it is not, there is no freed budget and no build. (2) With the budget freed, stack Intelligence and re-measure damage - the 1.25 to 1.625 scalar is additive baseline damage, so it should show up as a clean percentage and can be checked rather than assumed. (3) Blood Lance is the Overpower *spender* in the meta build's loop; check what happens to the Bloodbath legendary node and the Dominate glyph when it becomes the spender and the gainer at once, because that loop was designed around two skills and this build has one. (4) Compare against necromancer-meta-blood-wave on the PTR at equal gear, on packs and on a single target. (5) Re-check everything at launch: 3.2.0 is a test build and the scalar is exactly the kind of number that moves between PTR and release.
